scope_verdict: PLAY. All eight lesson bodies teach Simon Stephens's 2012 stage adaptation, not Haddon's novel: Act 1 and Act 2, Siobhan reading Christopher's book aloud, the ensemble, Frantic Assembly, the graph-paper set, the post-curtain maths scene. Lessons 1, 6 and 8 explicitly warn students never to mention chapters. Only the titles of lessons 2, 3 and 4 still carry the novel's prime-numbered chapter ranges (finding F13). No rebuild is needed; the unit needs three title changes.

findings.claim: AO4 - "the requirement to show understanding of the relationships between texts and the contexts in which they were written, performed, and received".
findings.truth: That is AO3. AO4 is "use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation". It is worth 5 of the 40 marks on this question. Lesson 8 already defines AO4 correctly, so the unit contradicted itself.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md section 3.1 (AO list) and section 2.2 (Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4).

findings.claim: "For AO4 in your exam, you should reference the theatrical context..." and "AO4 context should reference the 2012 National Theatre premiere...".
findings.truth: AO4 is spelling, punctuation, grammar and vocabulary. Context is AO3, and AO3 is not assessed on the post-1914 prose and drama question at all. A student who spends time on context to chase AO4 marks loses time for no credit.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md section 2.2: "Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4."

findings.claim: Practice question 2 stem: "...You should consider the context in which the play was written and performed."
findings.truth: Context earns no marks on this section. The real question is a source-based response assessing AO1, AO2 and AO4 only. The context instruction belongs to the 19th-century prose question, not this one.

findings.claim: Fifteen top-band descriptors across lessons 1-7 credit context under an "AO4:" label, e.g. "AO4: references 2012 National Theatre premiere... neurodiversity discourse of 2012" and "AO4: context of a single parent raising a child with additional needs in Swindon".
findings.truth: AO4 is the writing-accuracy objective. Context is AO3 and is not assessed here. The label was relabelled to say plainly that the background earns no marks but sharpens the reading.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md sections 2.2 and 3.1. Affects L1 Q1-Q4, L2 Q3/Q6, L3 Q1/Q4, L4 Q2/Q4, L5 Q1/Q3, L6 Q3/Q4, L7 Q5.

findings.claim: "Christopher achieves an A*" (repeated in the key fact, the conclusion, a flashcard, a practice-question stem, a glossary entry, a heading, and "achieves the highest possible result"). Also in the L8 practice scheme ("the A* result").
findings.truth: Christopher gets an A grade. The A* did not exist at A level when the novel was written, and the play follows the novel on this point.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/the-curious-incident-of-the-dog-in-the-night-time/summary - "Christopher receives an A on his exam". Novel ch. 233.

findings.claim: "Prime numbers are what is left when you have taken all the patterns away" - given as a quotation in lessons 4, 5, 7 and 8 (prose, a flashcard, a fill knowledge check and a match knowledge check).
findings.truth: The real wording is "Prime numbers is what is left when you have taken all the patterns away." The non-standard "is" is Christopher's own grammar and is part of the quotation.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/the-curious-incident-of-the-dog-in-the-night-time - quote listed at p.15 as "Prime numbers is what is left when you have taken all the patterns away".

findings.claim: The post-curtain maths scene "has no equivalent in Haddon's novel, which merely narrates the A-level exam result in prose".
findings.truth: The novel prints the full proof as an appendix at the back. The same lesson says so two paragraphs later, so the unit contradicted itself.
findings.evidence: Haddon, The Curious Incident..., Appendix (the right-angled triangle proof); the lesson's own collapsible "Why Stage Mathematics?".

findings.claim: All 48 practice questions carried the ladder "Top band (29-35) / Mid-high band (22-28) / Mid band (15-21) / Lower-mid band (8-14) / Lower band (1-7)" - a 35-mark total with two non-house band names.
findings.truth: The question is worth 40 marks. Rescaled to five equal house bands: Top band (33-40), Upper-mid band (25-32), Mid band (17-24), Lower-mid band (9-16), Low band (1-8).
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md section 2.2: "Section A (20%) Post 1914 Prose/Drama (40 marks)".

findings.claim: The board is named 14 times in lesson fields ("For your Eduqas GCSE", "Key Quotations for the Eduqas Exam", "In the Eduqas exam...", a knowledge-check stem, a flashcard stem, two descriptions), and lesson 8 carries the banned string "Component 2 Section A".
findings.truth: House rule for Eduqas/WJEC: lesson prose uses neutral phrasing and never names the board or a component/section code.
findings.evidence: scripts/_retrofc/CHECK_PROMPT.md banned-string list; house rule for Eduqas/WJEC lessons.

findings.claim: "In the your written exam exam, you will be given...", "your written exam gives you an extract...", "The your written exam question gives you..." (lessons 1 and 8).
findings.truth: Broken sentences left by an earlier automated de-boarding edit. Rewritten as clean sentences.
findings.evidence: raw/L01.txt n19 and n20; raw/L08.txt n26.

findings.claim: Seven of the eight descriptions are cut mid-phrase or mid-word, several ending with a stray ",." (e.g. "...Christopher begins his investigation, Mrs.").
findings.truth: Rewritten as complete sentences under 100 characters. Lessons 1-8 except lesson 2's body text.

findings.claim: Five one-word flashcard answers ("Fifteen.", "Two.", "2012.", "Seven.", "Five.") on How old / How many / In which year questions, plus one bare comma-list answer ("Consistent rules, verifiable proofs and definite answers.").
findings.truth: House validator rejects both shapes. Rewritten as short sentences.
findings.evidence: Flashcard rules in the unit brief; L2[2], L4[1], L6[0], L7[13], L8[9], L8[11], L8[12].

findings.claim: Lesson titles 2, 3 and 4 are "Chapters 2-89: Wellington's Murder", "Chapters 97-157: The Journey to London" and "Chapters 163-233: Truth & Resolution".
findings.truth: The set text is Stephens's play, which has two acts and no chapters. The lesson bodies teach Act 1 and Act 2 correctly and lessons 1, 6 and 8 explicitly tell students never to mention chapters - so the titles contradict the teaching. Suggested: "Act 1: Wellington's Murder", "Act 2: The Journey to London", "Act 2: Truth & Resolution". Titles are not editable through _edits.json.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md section 2.2 prescribes "The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night Time (play script) (Stephens)"; raw/L06.txt n2 ("Simon Stephens's play is structured in two acts").

findings.claim: 47 of the 48 practice questions are whole-text essay stems ("How does Stephens present...?"). Only L1 Q6 supplies an extract frame.
findings.truth: The real question is a single source-based response: a printed extract from the play plus the whole text. Students who only ever practise whole-text essays never rehearse working from a printed extract, which is where most of the AO2 marks are won. Two options: (a) re-author each stem as "In this extract... How does Stephens present X here and in the play as a whole?", which needs an extract chosen per question and is a build job, not a fact-check edit; (b) leave the stems and add an extract-handling section to lesson 8. Recommendation: (a) for lessons 2-4 and 8 at least, since those are the plot and technique lessons. ORCHESTRATOR: stems left for the relabel/authoring workstream (source-based extracts need authoring).
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md section 2.2: "This assessment will test, through a source based response...".

findings.claim: Lesson 2 places the discovery of the letters as "Act 1's Climax" and lesson 3 opens "Act 2 opens in the aftermath of Christopher's discovery of the hidden letters... Ed... confesses". A knowledge check asks "What two things does Ed confess to in Act 2?".
findings.truth: I could not verify the act boundary in the Methuen script. Several accounts of the National Theatre production place Ed's confession at the end of Act One, immediately before the interval, not at the start of Act Two. If that is right, the lesson 3 heading and the knowledge-check stem send students to the wrong act. Options: check the published script and, if the confession closes Act One, move the confession material to lesson 2 and re-stem the knowledge check; or leave it if the script confirms Act Two. Recommendation: check the script before the next narration pass, since this ripples through two lessons. ORCHESTRATOR: act placement unverifiable without the Methuen script; left as NOTE.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia's play article gives no act divisions; the play-specific script was not available to fetch. Unverified either way.

findings.claim: Judy's letter is quoted as "I am not a very good mother, Christopher. Maybe if things had been different... maybe if you'd been different... but that is not your fault." and lesson 8 lists it as "reliably attested in the play-text". Lesson 5 quotes it and a fill knowledge check tests "but that is not _____ fault".
findings.truth: I could not find this wording in any source. LitCharts' account of the letters paraphrases "She doesn't think she's a very good mother, because she's impatient and gets upset easily" - no "that is not your fault" clause. The line reads like a conflation of two passages. It may still be right, so it is not edited, but it should be checked against the script before a student memorises it. The "reliably attested" claim has been softened in lesson 8.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/the-curious-incident-of-the-dog-in-the-night-time/chapter-157 (paraphrase only); the wording is absent from LitCharts and GradeSaver quote pages.

findings.claim: The Siobhan line appears as "...she tells me exactly what it is I am not allowed to do. I like this." in lessons 5 and 8, but as "...what it is I'm not allowed to do" in a lesson 1 mark scheme.
findings.truth: Two renderings of one quotation. The novel wording is close to "...she tells me exactly what it is that I am not allowed to do. And I like this." I could not confirm the exact words, so nothing is edited, but the unit should settle on one rendering.
findings.evidence: raw/L01.txt practice Q3; raw/L05.txt n16; raw/L08.txt n23. Wording unverified.

findings.claim: The play's final line is given as "Does that mean I can do anything Siobhan?" everywhere except the lesson 8 conclusion, which drops the name: "Does that mean I can do anything?".
findings.truth: One of the two is wrong, and no source I could reach prints the line. There is also no comma before the vocative in the version used across the unit. Settle the wording against the script.
findings.evidence: raw/L04.txt n11/n12, raw/L08.txt n22 vs raw/L08.txt n36. Wording unverified.

summary: The unit teaches the play, so it is fit for the set text. The real damage was in the exam claims: AO4 was defined and used as context in lesson 1 when AO4 is spelling, punctuation, grammar and vocabulary, and context (AO3) is not assessed on this section at all - that error also drove fifteen top-band descriptors and one question stem. Christopher's A-level result was given as an A* in eight places when it is an A. All 48 practice ladders topped out at 35 marks instead of 40 and used non-house band names. The board was named 14 times in lesson prose against the house rule, and 'Component 2 Section A' appeared once. 101 edits; three quotations could not be verified and are recorded as notes.
